title: How Anti-matter Spacecraft Will Work
summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Bizarro World and the idea of anti-matter, then explain matter and anti-matter (positrons, anti-protons, anti-hydrogen), Paul Dirac's equation, Carl Anderson's cloud chamber discovery of the positron, CERN and Fermilab experiments, the matter-antimatter asymmetry problem, and the challenges of producing, storing, and using antimatter as spacecraft propulsion (cost, magnetic storage rings, radiation, g-forces). The back half is a listener mail segment in which comedian John Hodgman appears as a guest and reads from and promotes his book That Is All, plus a joking Diners Club card pitch. The episode ends with a sign-off and a promo for the Stuff from the Future video podcast.

segments.title: Opening banter and Bizarro World
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about nicknames and the Flash, then discuss Bizarro World (Htrae), its DC Comics origins, and how its premise loosely relates to the idea of antimatter.

segments.title: Matter, atoms, and antimatter basics
segments.summary: The hosts review atomic structure (nucleus, protons, neutrons, electrons) and explain that antimatter particles have the same mass but opposite charge, giving examples such as positrons and anti-protons.

segments.title: Dirac's equation and Anderson's positron discovery
segments.summary: Paul Dirac revised Einstein's mass-energy equation to include a plus or minus sign, implying antimatter. Carl Anderson later photographed evidence of the positron using a cloud chamber in a magnetic field.

segments.title: Antimatter production at CERN, Berkeley and particle accelerators
segments.summary: The hosts describe how particle accelerators smash particles together to create antimatter, noting CERN's creation of anti-hydrogen atoms that lasted about forty nanoseconds and the discovery of anti-protons at the Berkeley Bevatron.

segments.title: Annihilation and the energy it releases
segments.summary: When matter and antimatter meet they annihilate into pure energy, which the hosts describe as the most efficient known reaction, with nearly all mass converted, compared with nuclear fusion.

segments.title: Matter-antimatter asymmetry problem
segments.summary: The standard theory predicts equal amounts of matter and antimatter after the Big Bang, which conflicts with the existence of matter today. Explanations include a slight asymmetry, measured by CERN's NA48 and Fermilab's KTeV experiments, and possible antimatter stores at the galactic center.

segments.title: Antimatter production costs and propulsion potential
segments.summary: Production so far totals under a millionth of a gram, with costs estimated at over a thousand trillion dollars per gram at current rates. The hosts note antimatter releases far more energy per kilogram than TNT or chemical rockets and could cut a Mars trip from about eleven months to one month.

segments.title: Storage, engine design, and challenges
segments.summary: The hosts outline three components of an antimatter engine (storage, feeding, and a magnetic rocket nozzle). They discuss CERN storing anti-hydrogen for about 1000 seconds, charge repulsion limiting storage, Steve Howe's fission-based sail idea, gamma radiation hazards, and whether humans could survive the high g-forces.

segments.title: Closing thoughts on antimatter spacecraft
segments.summary: The hosts conclude that antimatter spacecraft may arrive in coming decades and point listeners to the website's search for more on the topic.

segments.title: Listener mail from Sarah and John Hodgman's visit
segments.summary: A listener letter from Sarah is read, and John Hodgman appears in studio, jokingly describing his 'deranged millionaire' persona, reading from his book That Is All, and promoting a joke Diners Club card pitch.

segments.title: Sign-off and promotions
segments.summary: The hosts invite questions for Hodgman via Twitter and Facebook and email, and promote the Stuff from the Future video podcast.
